questions.question: What is the Azure Shared Responsibility Model?
options: Shared equally regardless of service type
Microsoft manages physical infrastructure; customer responsibility varies by service model (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS)
questions.explanation: In IaaS you manage OS and up; in PaaS Microsoft manages more; in SaaS Microsoft manages almost everything. The datacenter, network, and physical hosts are always Microsoft's responsibility.

questions.question: Which Azure service provides scalable object/blob storage?
questions.explanation: Azure Blob Storage is optimized for storing massive amounts of unstructured data like images, videos, backups, and logs. It supports hot, cool, and archive access tiers.

questions.question: What is an Azure Region?
options: A set of datacenters deployed within a latency-defined perimeter, connected via a dedicated low-latency network
A worldwide network of CDN nodes
questions.explanation: An Azure Region is a geographic area containing one or more datacenters (Availability Zones) connected by a low-latency network. Examples: East US, West Europe.

questions.question: What is an Azure Availability Zone?
options: A redundancy option for Azure Blob Storage
Physically separate datacenters within a region with independent power, cooling, and networking
questions.explanation: Availability Zones are physically separate locations within a region. They protect against datacenter failures. Each zone has independent power, cooling, and networking.

questions.question: Which cloud model gives you the most control over the underlying infrastructure?
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides VMs, storage, and networking — you control the OS, runtime, and applications. PaaS and SaaS abstract more of the infrastructure.

questions.question: What is Azure Active Directory (Azure AD / Entra ID)?
options: Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service
questions.explanation: Azure Active Directory (now Microsoft Entra ID) is a cloud-based IAM service providing authentication, single sign-on (SSO), multi-factor authentication, and conditional access.

questions.question: What is the Azure pricing benefit of using Reserved Virtual Machine Instances?
options: No benefit; pay-as-you-go is always cheaper
Up to 72% savings vs pay-as-you-go for 1 or 3-year commitments
questions.explanation: Azure Reserved VM Instances provide up to 72% cost savings compared to pay-as-you-go pricing when you commit to 1 or 3 years for predictable workloads.

questions.question: What is Azure Resource Manager (ARM)?
options: The deployment and management service that provides a consistent management layer for Azure resources
questions.explanation: ARM is the management layer for Azure. All Azure management tools (portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs) go through ARM. It enables RBAC, tagging, locks, and template-based deployments.

questions.question: What is a benefit of the public cloud over on-premises infrastructure?
options: Eliminates capital expenditure — shifts to operational expenditure (OpEx)
questions.explanation: Cloud shifts IT spending from CapEx (upfront hardware) to OpEx (pay-as-you-go). You don't buy servers; you pay for services consumed.

questions.question: Which Azure service provides serverless code execution?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service. You write event-driven code and pay only for execution time. No server management required.

questions.question: What is Azure Defender (Microsoft Defender for Cloud)?
options: A unified security management system that provides threat protection across Azure, on-premises, and other clouds
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud provides unified security management and advanced threat protection. It assesses security posture and detects threats across hybrid environments.

questions.question: What is the Azure SLA (Service Level Agreement)?
options: A formal commitment by Microsoft to provide a minimum level of service availability (e.g., 99.9%)
questions.explanation: Azure SLAs define the minimum uptime guarantees for each service. If Microsoft misses the SLA, customers receive service credits. Most services offer 99.9% to 99.99% SLAs.

questions.question: Which Azure tool lets you estimate costs before deploying resources?
questions.explanation: The Azure Pricing Calculator lets you configure services and estimate monthly costs before deployment. Azure Cost Management analyzes actual spending.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Policy?
options: Enforce organizational standards and assess compliance at scale across Azure resources
questions.explanation: Azure Policy helps enforce rules (e.g., 'all VMs must use managed disks', 'resources must be tagged') and evaluates compliance of existing resources.

questions.question: What is a Hybrid Cloud?
options: Combining on-premises/private cloud with public cloud services
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud combines on-premises or private cloud infrastructure with public cloud services, allowing data and applications to move between environments.

questions.question: What does Azure Advisor provide?
options: Personalized recommendations to optimize Azure resources for reliability, security, performance, and cost
questions.explanation: Azure Advisor analyzes your Azure usage and provides recommendations across 5 categories: reliability, security, performance, cost, and operational excellence.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Monitor?
options: Collect, analyze, and act on telemetry data (metrics and logs) from Azure and on-premises environments
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor collects metrics and logs from resources, enables alerts and autoscale, and integrates with other tools like Application Insights and Log Analytics.

questions.question: What is multi-factor authentication (MFA) in Azure AD?
options: Requiring users to verify identity using two or more verification methods (e.g., password + phone)
questions.explanation: MFA requires two or more verification factors: something you know (password), something you have (phone/authenticator app), or something you are (biometric). Significantly reduces breach risk.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Resource Groups?
options: A logical container for related Azure resources that share the same lifecycle, permissions, and policies
questions.explanation: Resource Groups are logical containers for organizing Azure resources. Resources in a group share lifecycle management — deploy, update, or delete them together.

questions.question: Which Azure service provides a managed relational database with compatibility for MySQL and PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: Azure Database for MySQL and Azure Database for PostgreSQL are fully managed open-source database services. Azure SQL Database is for Microsoft SQL Server workloads.

questions.question: What is Azure DevOps?
options: A set of developer services for planning (Boards), code (Repos), CI/CD pipelines, testing, and artifacts
questions.explanation: Azure DevOps provides integrated tools: Boards (Agile planning), Repos (Git), Pipelines (CI/CD), Test Plans, and Artifacts (package management). Used end-to-end for software development lifecycle.

questions.question: What is Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)?
options: A managed Kubernetes container orchestration service that removes the burden of managing the Kubernetes control plane
questions.explanation: AKS is a managed Kubernetes service. Azure manages the control plane (API server, etcd) for free; you manage and pay for worker nodes. Integrates with Azure AD, Monitor, and Container Registry.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure Scale Sets and standalone VMs?
options: Scale Sets automatically create/delete identical VM instances based on demand or a schedule
Scale Sets use different OS images
Scale Sets are only for Windows
questions.explanation: VM Scale Sets let you deploy and auto-scale a group of identical, load-balanced VMs. When demand increases, Scale Sets add VMs; when demand drops, they remove them — reducing manual management.

questions.question: What is Azure App Service?
options: A fully managed PaaS for hosting web applications, REST APIs, and mobile backends without managing server infrastructure
questions.explanation: App Service supports .NET, Node.js, Python, PHP, Java, and containers. Azure manages patching, scaling, and infrastructure. You deploy code or containers and configure scaling rules.

questions.question: What is Azure Cosmos DB?
options: A globally distributed, multi-model NoSQL database with guaranteed single-digit millisecond latency
questions.explanation: Cosmos DB supports multiple APIs (SQL/Core, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table). Data is replicated globally with configurable consistency levels. SLA: 99.999% availability.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Load Balancer vs Azure Application Gateway?
options: Load Balancer: Layer 4 (TCP/UDP) for VM-to-VM traffic. Application Gateway: Layer 7 (HTTP/S) with WAF, SSL termination, cookie affinity, and URL routing
Application Gateway is for internal traffic only
questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer operates at Layer 4 for internal or public VM traffic. Application Gateway is Layer 7 for web workloads — adds WAF, SSL offload, URL-path routing, and session affinity.

questions.question: What is Azure VPN Gateway?
options: Connects on-premises networks or individual clients to Azure Virtual Networks over encrypted tunnels (Site-to-Site, Point-to-Site, or VNet-to-VNet)
questions.explanation: VPN Gateway creates encrypted tunnels over the internet: S2S (site-to-site for branch offices), P2S (point-to-site for remote workers), VNet-to-VNet. For dedicated private connections, use ExpressRoute.

questions.question: What is Azure ExpressRoute?
options: A private, dedicated network connection from on-premises to Azure that bypasses the public internet, offering predictable performance and lower latency
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute provides dedicated connectivity through a partner provider — no public internet. Offers bandwidths from 50 Mbps to 100 Gbps. Ideal for compliance, consistent performance, and large data transfers.

questions.question: What is the Azure Trust Center?
options: A portal providing transparency about Microsoft's security, privacy, compliance practices, and data handling — including regulatory certifications
questions.explanation: The Azure Trust Center (and compliance.microsoft.com) documents Microsoft's compliance certifications (ISO, SOC, GDPR, HIPAA), privacy commitments, and security practices for enterprise customers.

questions.question: What is the difference between CapEx and OpEx in the context of cloud?
options: CapEx: upfront capital investment in hardware/infrastructure. OpEx: ongoing operational expenses. Cloud shifts IT spending from CapEx to OpEx (pay-as-you-go)
questions.explanation: Traditional IT: CapEx (buy servers, depreciate over time). Cloud: OpEx (pay monthly subscription/consumption). Cloud benefits: no upfront cost, scale up/down, stop paying when not needed.

questions.question: What is Azure Blueprints?
options: A design tool for network diagrams
A service that packages together resource groups, ARM templates, policies, role assignments, and subscriptions into repeatable, auditable compliance packages
questions.explanation: Azure Blueprints define a repeatable set of resources that implements and follows organizational standards. Unlike ARM templates, Blueprints track deployed resources and can be updated centrally.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure Portal, CLI, and PowerShell?
options: Three ways to manage Azure resources: Portal (web GUI), CLI (cross-platform command-line), PowerShell (Windows/cross-platform scripting). All call the same ARM API.
questions.explanation: All three management interfaces send requests to the Azure Resource Manager API. Portal: visual, good for exploration. CLI: script-friendly, cross-platform. PowerShell: powerful scripting, better for Windows admins.

questions.question: What is Azure Key Vault?
options: A cloud service for securely storing and managing secrets, encryption keys, and certificates, with access auditing
questions.explanation: Key Vault stores secrets (passwords, connection strings), encryption keys (HSM-backed), and certificates. Access is controlled via Azure AD and RBAC. Every access is logged for auditing.

questions.question: What is Azure Cost Management + Billing?
options: Provides visibility into actual Azure spend, enables budgets and alerts, shows spending trends, and helps identify cost optimization opportunities
questions.explanation: Azure Cost Management + Billing lets you analyze spending by resource, tag, department, or subscription; set budgets with alert notifications; and see recommendations for reducing costs.

questions.question: What is an Azure Subscription?
options: A logical container that holds Azure resources and defines billing, access control, and resource limits. One account can have multiple subscriptions
questions.explanation: Subscriptions are billing units in Azure. Each subscription has its own billing, limits, and RBAC. Organizations often use separate subscriptions for dev, test, and production environments.

questions.question: What is Azure Sentinel (Microsoft Sentinel)?
options: A cloud-native SIEM + SOAR solution for collecting, detecting, investigating, and responding to security threats across the enterprise
questions.explanation: Microsoft Sentinel collects data at cloud scale, uses ML for threat detection, provides investigation tools, and enables automated responses (playbooks). Replaces traditional on-premises SIEM.

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Resource Tags?
options: Metadata name-value pairs applied to resources for organization, cost allocation, automation, and access control
questions.explanation: Tags (e.g., 'Environment:Production', 'Owner:TeamA') enable cost reporting by department, automated policies, lifecycle management, and resource organization across subscriptions.

questions.question: What is Azure Service Health?
options: Provides personalized alerts about Azure service incidents, maintenance, and health advisories affecting your specific resources and regions
questions.explanation: Service Health provides three feeds: Service Issues (active incidents), Planned Maintenance (scheduled work), and Health Advisories. Customized to your subscriptions and regions with alert rules.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure AD Free and Azure AD Premium?
options: Premium P1/P2 adds: Conditional Access, Identity Protection, Privileged Identity Management (PIM), self-service password reset, MFA per-user enforcement, and advanced reporting
Premium is only for enterprise accounts
questions.explanation: Azure AD Free: basic SSO, MFA for administrators. Premium P1: Conditional Access, hybrid identity. Premium P2: Identity Protection (risky sign-ins), Privileged Identity Management (just-in-time access).

questions.question: What is the Azure Well-Architected Framework?
options: Microsoft's guidance for designing reliable, secure, efficient, and cost-effective Azure solutions across 5 pillars: Reliability, Security, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, Performance Efficiency
questions.explanation: The Azure Well-Architected Framework provides best practices across 5 pillars to evaluate architecture quality. The Azure Advisor tool surfaces actionable recommendations aligned to these pillars.

questions.question: What is Azure Cognitive Services?
options: A collection of AI APIs (vision, speech, language, decision) that enable apps to see, hear, speak, understand, and decide without ML expertise
questions.explanation: Azure Cognitive Services provides pre-built AI capabilities via REST APIs: Computer Vision, Face, Speech-to-Text, Text Analytics, Translator, and more. No ML training required.

questions.question: What is Azure Machine Learning?
options: A cloud-based platform for training, deploying, and managing machine learning models at scale
questions.explanation: Azure ML provides MLOps capabilities: experiment tracking, automated ML, model registry, pipelines, and deployment to real-time or batch inference endpoints. Supports Python, R, and popular ML frameworks.

questions.question: What is Azure IoT Hub?
options: A managed cloud service for bidirectional communication between IoT devices and Azure — enables device management, telemetry ingestion, and commands
questions.explanation: Azure IoT Hub connects, monitors, and manages millions of IoT devices. Supports MQTT, AMQP, HTTPS. Enables device-to-cloud telemetry and cloud-to-device commands with device twin state management.

questions.question: What is Azure Cognitive Search?
options: An AI-powered cloud search service that indexes content from various sources and adds AI enrichment (OCR, entity extraction, translation) for rich search experiences
questions.explanation: Azure Cognitive Search (now Azure AI Search) provides full-text search with AI enrichment pipelines. Can index documents, images, and structured data, adding semantic search, vector search, and AI-extracted metadata.

questions.question: What is Azure Synapse Analytics?
options: An integrated analytics service combining enterprise data warehousing (SQL Pools) with big data analytics (Apache Spark) in a unified experience
questions.explanation: Azure Synapse integrates data warehousing, big data, and data integration. Dedicated SQL Pools for DW, Apache Spark for big data, integrated Pipelines for ETL, and Power BI connectivity.

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure Public, Private, and Hybrid cloud?
options: Public: Microsoft-managed shared infrastructure. Private: dedicated Azure Stack or on-premises. Hybrid: combination of public Azure + on-premises/private cloud connected via VPN or ExpressRoute
questions.explanation: Public cloud: shared, multi-tenant, Microsoft-owned. Private cloud: dedicated hardware (Azure Dedicated Host) or Azure Stack Hub on-premises. Hybrid: connects both, enabling workload portability.

questions.question: What is Azure Lighthouse?
options: Enables managed service providers (MSPs) and enterprises to manage multiple Azure tenants and subscriptions from a single control plane
questions.explanation: Azure Lighthouse provides cross-tenant management. MSPs can manage customer environments without logging into each tenant separately. Customers maintain full visibility and control over delegated access.

questions.question: What is Azure Arc?
options: Extends Azure management and services to any infrastructure — on-premises servers, other clouds, or edge — managed through the Azure portal
questions.explanation: Azure Arc brings Azure's management (RBAC, Policy, Monitor, Defender) to non-Azure resources: on-premises servers, Kubernetes clusters on AWS/GCP, and Azure Stack Edge. Enables consistent governance everywhere.

questions.question: What is the Azure Free Account?
options: Provides $200 credit for 30 days + 12 months of popular free services + always-free services (25+ products) for new Azure customers
questions.explanation: Azure Free Account: $200 credit for 30 days exploration, 12 months free for popular services (B1S VM, 5 GB Blob Storage, etc.), plus 55+ always-free services like Azure Functions (1M requests/month).

questions.question: What is Azure Stack?
options: A family of products extending Azure services to edge and disconnected environments: Stack Hub (on-premises full Azure), Stack Edge (AI at edge), Stack HCI (hyper-converged)
questions.explanation: Azure Stack Hub: full Azure services in your datacenter for disconnected/regulatory scenarios. Stack Edge: AI-enabled appliance for edge computing. Stack HCI: hyper-converged infrastructure running Azure services locally.

questions.question: What is Azure Content Delivery Network (CDN)?
options: A distributed server network that caches static web content at edge nodes globally, reducing latency for users worldwide
questions.explanation: Azure CDN caches content (images, CSS, JS, videos) at Points of Presence (PoPs) close to users. Reduces origin server load and delivery latency. Partners: Microsoft, Verizon, Akamai (now converging to Microsoft CDN).

questions.question: What is Azure Service Bus?
options: A fully managed enterprise message broker with queues and publish-subscribe topics for reliable, asynchronous communication between distributed applications
questions.explanation: Azure Service Bus provides enterprise messaging: queues (point-to-point), topics/subscriptions (pub/sub). Supports FIFO, sessions, deferred processing, dead-letter queues, and at-least-once delivery.

questions.question: What is Azure Bot Service?
options: A platform for building, testing, deploying, and managing intelligent chatbots across multiple channels (Teams, Slack, web, Cortana)
A virtual assistant for Azure management
questions.explanation: Azure Bot Service provides a framework for building conversational AI bots. Integrates with Azure Cognitive Services (LUIS/CLU for NLP, QnA Maker/Knowledge Base for FAQ). Deployed to multiple channels.

questions.question: What is Azure Sphere?
options: An end-to-end IoT security solution combining a custom microcontroller (MCU), Linux OS, and cloud security service for secured connected devices
questions.explanation: Azure Sphere is Microsoft's hardware-software IoT security platform: custom MCU with security features, hardened Linux OS, and the Azure Sphere Security Service for OTA updates and certificate management.

questions.question: What is the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)?
options: A collection of documentation, guidance, best practices, and tools for organizations planning, implementing, and operating Azure at scale
questions.explanation: CAF provides proven guidance for Azure adoption: Strategy, Plan, Ready (landing zones), Migrate, Innovate, Secure, Manage, and Govern phases. Helps organizations move to Azure systematically and reduce risk.

questions.question: What is Azure DevTest Labs?
options: A service enabling developers to quickly provision dev/test environments with reusable templates, cost controls, and automatic shutdown to minimize waste
questions.explanation: DevTest Labs lets teams create on-demand VMs and environments from pre-approved templates with cost thresholds, auto-shutdown policies, and claiming/reclaiming capabilities — reducing dev/test spending.

questions.question: What does 'lift and shift' migration mean in Azure?
options: Migrating on-premises VMs/applications to Azure IaaS with minimal changes — taking advantage of cloud economics without re-architecting
questions.explanation: Lift and shift (rehost) = move as-is to IaaS. Fastest migration approach. Other strategies: replatform (minor optimizations), refactor/re-architect (redesign for cloud-native), rebuild (start fresh), replace (SaaS).

questions.question: What is Azure Spring Apps?
options: A fully managed platform for running Spring Boot microservices applications, handling infrastructure, scaling, monitoring, and CI/CD integration
questions.explanation: Azure Spring Apps (developed with VMware/Broadcom) provides a fully managed Spring runtime. Developers focus on code; Azure manages the underlying infrastructure, networking, and service discovery.

questions.question: What is the Azure Security Benchmark?
options: Microsoft's security guidance aligned with industry standards (CIS, NIST), providing prescriptive best practices for securing Azure services
A performance benchmark for Azure VMs
questions.explanation: The Azure Security Benchmark (now Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark) provides prioritized security recommendations for Azure aligned with CIS Controls and NIST SP 800-53. Used as a baseline in Defender for Cloud.

questions.question: What is Azure Applied AI Services?
options: Purpose-built AI services for common scenarios: Form Recognizer (document processing), Metrics Advisor (anomaly detection), Video Analyzer, Immersive Reader, Bot Service
questions.explanation: Applied AI Services are higher-level solutions built on Cognitive Services for specific business scenarios. They require less customization than building from scratch with raw Cognitive Services APIs.

questions.question: What is Azure Availability Sets vs Availability Zones?
options: Availability Sets: protect from hardware failures within a data center (separate fault and update domains). Availability Zones: protect from entire data center failure — physically separate buildings with independent power/cooling
questions.explanation: Availability Sets (2+ VMs): 99.95% SLA — distributes VMs across fault domains (separate racks) and update domains. Availability Zones (3 zones in a region): 99.99% SLA — separate buildings, better protection.

questions.question: What is Azure Batch?
options: A managed service for running large-scale parallel and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads — automatically provisions, manages, and scales compute nodes
questions.explanation: Azure Batch handles the infrastructure for HPC and batch jobs: provision compute pools, schedule jobs, retry failed tasks. Pay for VMs used. Ideal for 3D rendering, simulation, genomics, financial modeling.

questions.question: What is Azure Managed Disks vs Unmanaged Disks?
options: Managed Disks: Azure manages storage accounts, replication, and redundancy automatically. Unmanaged Disks: you manage storage accounts manually (legacy). Managed Disks is the recommended approach for all new workloads
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Disks handle storage account management, capacity planning, and redundancy automatically. Support encryption, backup (snapshots, Azure Backup), and role-based access. Types: Ultra Disk, Premium SSD, Standard SSD, Standard HDD.

questions.question: What is the Azure Policy Deny effect?
options: Prevents resource deployment that violates policy rules — unlike Audit which just reports non-compliance, Deny actively blocks creation or modification of non-compliant resources
questions.explanation: Azure Policy effects: Deny (block), Audit (log), Append (add fields), Modify (alter properties), DeployIfNotExists (deploy remediation), AuditIfNotExists (audit if related resource missing). Deny is the most restrictive.

questions.question: What is the Azure Well-Architected Review?
options: A free self-assessment tool in the Azure portal that evaluates workloads against the Well-Architected Framework pillars and provides prioritized recommendations
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Review asks 50+ questions about your workload across the 5 pillars. Results show your score per pillar and recommendations prioritized by impact. Helps identify architectural risks and improvement areas.

questions.question: What is Azure DevTest Labs?
options: A service that provides self-service sandboxes for developers and testers with reusable VM templates, cost controls, and automatic shutdown — prevents wasteful spending in dev/test environments
questions.explanation: DevTest Labs lets teams spin up dev/test environments quickly using templates. Features: auto-shutdown policies to save costs, spending caps, claimable VMs, artifact library (install software automatically).

questions.question: What is the difference between Azure Tenant and Azure Subscription?
options: Each subscription has its own AD
A subscription is bigger than a tenant
Tenant: a dedicated Azure AD instance representing your organization (identity boundary). Subscription: a billing and resource container within a tenant. One tenant can have multiple subscriptions
questions.explanation: Azure AD Tenant: created when your organization signs up for Azure — owns user identities. Subscription: billing container for resources, associated with one tenant. Multiple subscriptions can share one tenant (common for large organizations).

questions.question: What is Azure Monitor Metrics vs Azure Monitor Logs?
options: Logs are stored for less time than Metrics

Metrics: numerical time-series data (CPU %, requests/sec) stored for 93 days by default, near real-time, optimized for dashboards and alerts. Logs: structured/unstructured event data in Log Analytics workspace, queried with KQL
questions.explanation: Metrics: lightweight, fast, great for real-time alerts and dashboards. Logs (Log Analytics): rich query capability with KQL, long retention, can combine data from many sources (VMs, apps, security, network).

questions.question: What is the purpose of Azure Reserved VM Instances?
options: Lock in a specific IP address
1 or 3-year commitment to a specific VM type/region in exchange for up to 72% savings vs pay-as-you-go — ideal for predictable, steady-state workloads
questions.explanation: Reserved VM Instances (RIs) offer significant cost savings for steady workloads: Standard RI (fixed size), Convertible RI (can change size/series). Commitment: 1yr (~40% off) or 3yr (~72% off). Can be exchanged or sold.

questions.question: What does 'Infrastructure as a Service' (IaaS) mean in Azure?
options: Azure provides: virtualized hardware (VMs, networking, storage). Customer manages: OS, middleware, runtime, data, applications. Example: Azure Virtual Machines
questions.explanation: IaaS: rent compute, network, storage infrastructure. You manage: OS patches, runtime, applications. Examples: Azure VMs, Virtual Networks, Azure Storage. Compare PaaS (Azure manages OS too) and SaaS (managed entirely).

questions.question: What is Azure Private Endpoint?
options: A network interface with a private IP from your VNet that connects privately to an Azure service (Storage, Key Vault, SQL) — traffic stays on Azure backbone, never touches internet
questions.explanation: Private Endpoints create a NIC in your VNet for an Azure service. DNS resolves the service name to the private IP. Traffic from your VNet never leaves the Azure network. Enables strict private connectivity for compliance.

questions.question: What is the Azure Free Account?
options: Only one month of free services
12 months of popular services free, $200 credit for 30 days to explore all services, and 55+ always-free services (Functions, Blob Storage, Cosmos DB, SQL Database at limited tiers)
Requires a credit card but never charged
questions.explanation: Azure Free Account: $200 credit for 30 days (explore any service), 12 months free for popular services (VMs, Blob, SQL), and permanently free tiers for services like Functions (1M executions/month), Cosmos DB (400 RU/s), and others.

questions.question: What is Azure Update Manager?
options: A unified service to manage and govern OS updates across Azure VMs, Azure Arc-enabled servers, and on-premises — view compliance status, schedule maintenance windows, deploy updates at scale
questions.explanation: Azure Update Manager (formerly Update Management in Automation) provides a centralized dashboard for update compliance and deployment across Windows/Linux VMs. Supports Azure VMs, Arc-enabled servers, and on-premises.

questions.question: What is the Microsoft Purview compliance portal?
options: A unified compliance and risk management platform including Compliance Manager, Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, eDiscovery, and Communication Compliance for Microsoft 365 and Azure
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview combines compliance features: Compliance Manager (regulatory compliance score and tracking), Information Protection (classify/label data), DLP (prevent data leaks), eDiscovery (legal holds), Insider Risk Management.

questions.question: What is Azure Security Center / Microsoft Defender for Cloud?
options: A unified security management and threat protection platform providing security posture management (Secure Score), threat detection, and workload protection across Azure, on-premises, and multi-cloud
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Security Center + Azure Defender): Free tier provides Secure Score and basic recommendations. Paid tier adds threat protection for servers, storage, SQL, containers, Key Vault, and more.

questions.question: What is the Azure CLI and how does it differ from PowerShell?
options: Azure CLI only works on Linux

Azure CLI (az): cross-platform Bash-friendly command line tool. Azure PowerShell (Az module): PowerShell cmdlets, ideal for Windows admins. Both call Azure Resource Manager API — choose based on scripting preference
questions.explanation: Azure CLI: az commands, great for Bash scripts and Linux/Mac, simple syntax. Azure PowerShell: Az cmdlets, powerful for Windows scripting, integrates with Windows automation. Both are cross-platform and call the same ARM API.

questions.question: What is Azure Arc?
options: Extends Azure management to on-premises, multi-cloud, and edge resources — enabling Azure Policy, RBAC, Defender for Cloud, and Azure Monitor on servers/Kubernetes clusters outside Azure
questions.explanation: Azure Arc registers non-Azure resources (on-premises VMs, AWS/GCP VMs, Kubernetes clusters) in Azure as Arc-enabled resources. Enables consistent governance, security, and management across environments using Azure tools.

questions.question: What is the Azure Marketplace?
options: A catalog of thousands of certified applications, services, and solutions from Microsoft and partners (VMs, containers, SaaS, professional services) that can be deployed directly to Azure
questions.explanation: Azure Marketplace offers: VM images (pre-configured with software like SAP, Oracle, Palo Alto), SaaS applications, development tools, security solutions, and professional services. Some are free, others have per-hour or per-seat pricing.

questions.question: What is Azure Container Registry (ACR)?
options: A managed, private Docker container registry in Azure for storing and managing container images and Helm charts — integrates with AKS and ACI for secure container deployments
questions.explanation: ACR is Azure's private container registry. Build and push images, sign them for security, use geo-replication for global distribution. Integrates with CI/CD (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions) and deploys to AKS, ACI, App Service.

questions.question: What is the Azure Shared Responsibility Model for Platform as a Service (PaaS)?
options: Azure manages: infrastructure, OS, platform runtime, and middleware. Customer manages: applications, data, user access, and some network configurations. Example: Azure App Service, Azure SQL Database
questions.explanation: PaaS responsibility: Azure handles physical security, hardware, OS, runtime/platform patching. You handle: application code, data, access management, client-side security. Middle ground between IaaS (manage OS) and SaaS (manage nothing).

questions.question: Your organization was using 'Azure Active Directory' for identity and access management. You notice Microsoft now refers to it by a new name in the portal and documentation. What is the current official name of this service?
questions.explanation: In 2023, Microsoft rebranded Azure Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID as part of the broader Microsoft Entra product family. The service capabilities (tenants, users, groups, Conditional Access, MFA) are unchanged — only the name and logos were updated.

questions.question: A cloud administrator wants an AI-powered assistant integrated directly into the Azure portal to help design architectures, write CLI commands, query resource health, and troubleshoot issues using natural language. Which Microsoft service provides this capability?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Copilot in Azure is an AI assistant embedded in the Azure portal that helps users design, operate, optimize, and troubleshoot Azure resources through natural-language prompts. Advisor gives recommendations but not conversational AI.

questions.question: A team needs to deploy GPT-4 and other OpenAI models in Azure with enterprise features such as private networking, content filtering, responsible AI controls, and regional data residency. Which Azure service should they use?
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI Service, now part of Azure AI Foundry, provides managed access to OpenAI models (GPT-4, GPT-4o, DALL-E, Whisper, embeddings) with Azure enterprise features: private endpoints, content filters, customer-managed keys, and regional deployments.

questions.question: A DevOps team wants a fully managed Grafana service in Azure to visualize metrics from Azure Monitor, Prometheus, and other data sources, with Entra ID authentication and workspace-level RBAC. Which service should they use?
questions.explanation: Azure Managed Grafana is a fully managed service that runs Grafana Enterprise in Azure. It integrates natively with Azure Monitor, supports Entra ID SSO, and provides workspace-level role assignments so teams can share dashboards securely.

questions.question: An enterprise is planning a large-scale migration to Azure and wants a prescriptive framework that covers strategy, planning, readiness, adoption, governance, and management — including pre-built 'landing zones' with baseline networking, identity, and security controls. Which Microsoft resource provides this?
options: Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) with Azure Landing Zones
questions.explanation: The Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) is Microsoft's end-to-end guidance for cloud adoption. Azure Landing Zones are CAF's reference implementations that provide a pre-configured, scalable foundation (management groups, policies, networking, identity) ready for workloads.

questions.question: Finance asks you to track Azure spending, set alert thresholds per subscription, and receive automatic recommendations to buy Reserved Instances or Savings Plans to lower costs. Which combination of Azure tools should you use?
options: Microsoft Cost Management with budgets, plus Azure Advisor cost recommendations
Azure Monitor metrics alerts on billing data
questions.explanation: Microsoft Cost Management provides cost analysis, budgets with alert thresholds, and forecasting. Azure Advisor's Cost category surfaces right-sizing, Reserved Instance, and Savings Plan recommendations based on usage patterns.

questions.question: A company runs Windows and Linux servers on-premises plus Kubernetes clusters in AWS. They want to manage all of these from the Azure portal using Azure Policy, tag governance, and Defender for Cloud — without migrating the workloads. Which Azure service enables this?
questions.explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure's control plane to resources outside Azure — servers, Kubernetes clusters, and data services on-premises or in other clouds. Once onboarded, they appear as Azure resources and can be governed by Azure Policy, RBAC, Defender for Cloud, and Azure Monitor.

questions.question: A healthcare customer must process encrypted data in memory so that not even the cloud provider or hypervisor admin can read it during computation. Which Azure capability addresses this requirement?
options: Azure Confidential Computing using Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs)
questions.explanation: Azure Confidential Computing protects data in use by running workloads inside hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (such as Intel SGX or AMD SEV-SNP). Data remains encrypted in memory and is inaccessible even to host administrators or the hypervisor.

questions.question: A data governance team needs a unified catalog that discovers, classifies, and tracks the lineage of data assets across Azure, on-premises SQL, AWS S3, and Power BI. Which service provides this?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview (formerly Azure Purview / Azure Data Catalog) is a unified data governance solution providing data discovery, automated classification, lineage tracking, and sensitivity labeling across multi-cloud and on-premises data estates.

questions.question: A developer wants to instrument a microservices application using the vendor-neutral OpenTelemetry standard and send traces, metrics, and logs to an Azure observability service with APM features like dependency maps and live metrics. Which service should they use?
options: Azure Monitor Application Insights (with OpenTelemetry distro)
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor Application Insights supports the OpenTelemetry standard via Microsoft's OpenTelemetry Distro, letting developers use vendor-neutral instrumentation while getting Application Insights features: application map, live metrics, failures, and end-to-end transaction diagnostics.
